rules.title: Santa Ana ban on algorithmic rent-pricing devices
rules.requirement: Prohibits the sale, licensing and use of algorithmic devices (automated or AI software) by landlords to set rental prices in Santa Ana. Landlords using the banned software may be fined $1,000.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords and apartment owners of residential rental property in Santa Ana; also covers the sale and licensing of algorithmic devices.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Whether the landlord uses software that qualifies as an 'Algorithmic Device' under the ordinance's definition

rules.penalty: Fine of $1,000; enforced mainly through the city's existing code enforcement system
rules.citation: Santa Ana ordinance prohibiting Algorithmic Devices (ordinance number and code section not given in source)
rules.quoted_span: Landlords caught using the banned software could be fined $1,000. The measure passed its first vote on Feb. 17, and Tuesday’s vote was the final step to officially put the ordinance into effect.
rules.conflict_note: Secondary news source (OCBJ, March 9, 2026). First reading Feb. 17, 2026; final adoption on the Tuesday before publication (likely March 3, 2026). The article does not give a specific effective date; California city ordinances typically take effect 30 days after adoption (around April 2026), so the rule is presumed in force by 2026-10-01. The Apartment Association of Orange County suggested possible legal liability and a role for recently adopted state regulations, which raises a possible preemption or legal-challenge question. No official citation is given.
